codeReview.summary: The session_title consumer is correctly placed before the default branch in the switch statement. It follows the established defensive pattern of checking conversation_id (redundant due to the early return at line 143, but consistent with settings_updated/mcp_status cases). The handler persists the title via IPC, syncs the tab name, and refreshes the sidebar — all without touching running/aiProcessing/turnFinishedRef. updateTabName is properly included in the useCallback deps array. The type assertion `message.data as { title: string }` follows the same pattern used by all other stream metadata event handlers in this file (mcp_auth, settings_updated, mcp_status). Tests are well-structured with proper mock isolation and cover all three validation assertions.

issues.description: The session_title handler does not call refreshConversationCache(conversation_id) after updating the title, whereas the manual rename path in useTitleRename.ts (line 78) does. If any component reads the conversation object from the SWR cache (via useSWR('conversation/{id}')), it will show a stale title until the next natural cache refresh. The sidebar refresh via emitter.emit('chat.history.refresh') re-fetches the conversation list separately, so the sidebar is fine. This is a potential staleness issue for components that consume the individual conversation SWR key.

The conversation_id guard `if (message.conversation_id === conversation_id)` is redundant — an identical check exists at line 143 as an early return that applies to all cases in the switch. This is consistent with settings_updated (line 358) and mcp_status cases, so it's a deliberate defensive pattern. Not a bug, just unnecessary code.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Stream metadata event handlers (session_title, settings_updated, mcp_status) all include a redundant conversation_id check inside their case body, even though the early return at line 143 already filters out mismatched conversations. This is a deliberate defensive pattern but is undocumented — future contributors may either (a) omit the check thinking it's unnecessary, or (b) waste time investigating why it exists.
